A calm place to count your steps and keep a simple walking record. No feed, no pressure.
Your steps stay on your phone
No account. No internet. No ads, no trackers. Nothing leaves the phone on its own; only a CSV you export yourself can.
A daily target gives the step ring something to fill.
8,000 steps is a common starting point. Change it later in Settings.
Sabeel uses height and weight only to estimate distance, energy and stride. Every field is optional.
You can change this any time in Settings.
Android asks for them separately. Sabeel opens without them, but counting steps needs activity recognition. Location is optional and asked only when you track a walk.
Sabeel does not request internet access, so nothing it records can leave your phone on its own.
Sabeel is built to keep your data where it belongs: on this phone.
The app does not request internet permission at all. Your steps, walks and routes cannot be uploaded, because there is nothing that can upload them.
There is no ad library, no advertising ID, no usage analytics and no crash reporter in Sabeel.
You never sign in. There is no server to sign in to.
Export your daily totals as a CSV file, or delete everything from Settings at any time. Both happen only when you tap them.
Reads the phone’s step counter so Sabeel can count steps. Nothing else is read.
Shows your daily reminder and a goal notification. Both can be turned off in Settings.
Used only while you are tracking a walk, to draw the route. It is not used in the background otherwise.
These are the only permissions Sabeel ever asks you for.

Distance, energy and active minutes are rough estimates derived from steps, height and weight. They are not medical measurements and not a diagnosis. Talk to a health professional about health decisions.
Sabeel is a small, offline step and walk journal. It stays quiet on purpose: no feed, no social pressure, no subscription.
Kotlin, Jetpack Compose and AndroidX, under the Apache 2.0 license. License notices are kept with the source of this app.
Sabeel is not a medical device and does not give health advice.

Use a goal from your routine?
Your median recorded day over the last four weeks was %1$s steps. A goal of %2$s steps stays close to that. You can change it any time.
Pauses your streak for today without breaking it. A rest day never adds a day.
Your streak stays where it is. Steps are still counted normally.
If the count looks low, this explains what to check.
Sabeel counts with the phone’s own step sensor. If the number looks low, one of these is usually the reason.
Without this permission Sabeel cannot read the step sensor at all. Allow it, then open Sabeel again.
Some phone makers stop apps in the background to save battery. These settings are the ones that usually matter.
Open Settings › Apps › Manage apps › Sabeel. Turn on Autostart, then set Battery saver to No restrictions.
Open Settings › Battery and device care › Battery › Background usage limits and make sure Sabeel is not in Sleeping apps. Then open Settings › Apps › Sabeel › Battery and choose Unrestricted.
Open Settings › Battery › App launch, find Sabeel and turn off automatic management. Then allow it to run in the background.
Open Settings › Battery › Battery optimization › All apps, find Sabeel and choose Don’t optimize. Also allow background activity in App info.
Open Settings › Battery › App battery management (or App optimization), find Sabeel and allow background activity. On some models it is in Settings › Apps › Sabeel › Battery.
Open Settings › Battery › Background power consumption management, find Sabeel and allow background power usage. Also allow auto-start in iManager.
Open Settings › Apps › Sabeel › Battery and choose Unrestricted. If your phone has an autostart or startup manager, allow Sabeel there too.
The step sensor only counts while the phone is with you and moving. Steps never leave the phone, so nothing can recover steps that were not counted.

Sabeel keeps a small foreground service running. Android or the phone maker can still stop it. Sabeel reconnects when you open the app and after your phone restarts, and it never invents a total to fill a gap.
Battery saver, a forced stop, or a restart can interrupt counting until Sabeel runs again.
A rest day never changes the counted steps; only the streak pauses.
This phone does not report a built-in step sensor, so no setting can turn counting on.
Wording and menus differ between phone models. These instructions are a guide, not a promise.
